memory_candidates.content: A line-shift repair tool that computes delta from a base revision to the working tree is NOT idempotent: running it twice applies the same delta twice, and a gate that only checks 'the citation lands on a non-blank line' will still pass, because a doubly-shifted citation usually lands on some other non-blank line. Two things make this easy to trip: the tool's convenient default of 'every file changed since the base' silently grows to include the citer files the first run rewrote, and a second pass aimed at a subset re-targets files the first pass already handled. The durable fix is a second, idempotent mode that rebuilds every citation from the base by CONTENT ALIGNMENT (difflib over the citer, mapped through the target's own base-to-now line map) rather than by arithmetic, and which can be rerun safely. Add it as the documented recovery route, not as a note.

When a bulk text pass uses a regex anchored on a bullet character, remember that markdown bold markers share it: `^\*` matches the first asterisk of `**Bold heading**:` as readily as the `*` of a list item. A 'tidy trailing punctuation inside list entries' pass silently rewrote 232 bold headings, one of which was a count-bearing, gate-pinned heading. The cheap and complete detector is to diff every touched file against the base revision and flag any line that differs ONLY by a stripped character - the same alignment then restores it. Run that detector after every mechanical pass, not only when something fails.

A plan's acceptance target can be wrong rather than unmet, and saying so with the arithmetic is the honest close. Two targets in this sweep were arithmetically inconsistent with the plan's own instructions: a bibliography entry count computed as the union of two key sets BEFORE the deduplication the same plan specifies, and a 'citations in the target form' floor derived from a research count of bibliographic citations that included inline prose ones the normal form does not govern. Do not force the number; report before/after, show the derivation of the correct figure, and name the check that actually evidences completeness (here: zero entries left in the old form, together with zero unresolvable keys).
